backa11eysa11y.text: BackA11eySa11y has been at this since 2016, and experience shows in the composure: the head-to-head tally lands near the summit, the resistance holds firm against the hardest hitters, and the lifetime exchange ratio runs top-shelf too. Against the toughest third, though, the grip loosens. The aim is sharp, headshots are few, and the lifetime IvI sits below the middle — a veteran whose matchup game outshines the career numbers.

bad1wolf.text: Bad1Wolf has been around since 2013, and the composure is earned: hard to kill, patient, and unbothered by stronger opposition. The matchup fighting sits above the middle without ever shouting about it, and a lifetime of duels backs that up. A veteran who wins by outlasting the other side, not by outrunning them.

bellanso.text: BellaNSO fights at a sprint: a top-tier tempo, a duel record among the very best, and bravery that holds as enemies get stronger. The very best opposition still finds cracks, the one glaring hole in a strong card. Everything else reads above average or better, and the lifetime board backs the matchups up.

butchberger.text: Butchberger has played since 2014, and the game is still sharp: a matchup board that reads above average, accurate shooting, and composed against tougher opposition. Headshots stay scarce, the kill pace sits in the middle, and the edge gives ground against the strongest third. A veteran whose card reads strong everywhere except the soft spots.

bix4ente.text: Bix4ente plays a front-foot game: above average in the matchups, brisk in tempo, and still pushing as the field toughens. The one-on-one outcomes land mid-pack, the lifetime ledger backs the matchups, and the headshot share stays above the middle. Nothing ornamental here, just a regular who keeps arriving ready.

balabolochka.text: BalabolOchka plays a polished, patient game: a clear step above the pack across the matchup card, with accuracy near the top and a headshot share sitting mid-pack. The win-loss arithmetic of their real fights sits high; the lifetime numbers back it up. The single wrinkle: against the hardest third, the edge wears thin. A steady regular with a sharp eye and a quiet game.

bethehero.text: BeTheHero has been fighting since 2018, and the card is a split portrait: a matchup rating well above average, resistance near the top, and their kill edge in real fights sits high. The accuracy and headshots both sit below average, and the lifetime board lands below average too, though the edge holds against the hardest third. The matchups tell a far kinder story than the lifetime numbers do. A veteran whose real fights outshine their record.

bullet6.text: Since 2016, BULLET6 has built a career on showing up: a matchup grade a notch above the middle, resistance that barely bends, and kill earnings in real fights sit high. The aim runs ordinary, and the lifetime board sits mid-pack. The hardest third is where the card thins — the consistency line dips under the middle there. A veteran regular, reliable as sunrise, still in the fight.

botvojes.text: BotVojes plays the whole game well: above average on the matchup rating, the tempo, the bravery, and the resistance, with nothing trailing far behind. The head-to-head reckoning lands mid-pack, while lifetime numbers paint a similar middling picture. Since 2023, a steady regular who rarely has a bad day on the battlefield.

blacktu.text: BlackTu plays a lopsided game: the matchups sit clearly above the middle, with a matchup kill tally well above average too, yet the edge collapses against the toughest third. The lifetime board reads below average, a cooler verdict than the matchups give, and the headshots land below average as well. A regular whose best fights are strong, but whose form wobbles when the opposition hardens.

blinddeafgunner.text: BlindDeafGunner is a puzzle with a sharp edge: head-to-head results sit just under the summit, and the rating stays clearly above the middle, yet lifetime marks, aim, and headshots all sit near the bottom. When the opposition gets toughest, the edge falls away, and bravery holds only mid-pack. A veteran whose best fights are elite, even if the rest refuses to follow.

bosopor.text: Bosopor plays a complete, high-tempo game: strong across the whole matchup board, with pace and output running hot. The aim is the standout — near the very top — with headshots above average and a matchup kill-death return well above average too. The lifetime board paints the same strong picture, and the edge holds steady against the toughest third.

bastyvs.text: BastyVS brings a complete, even game: a matchup rating sitting comfortably above the middle, fast between fights, and unshaken against better enemies. Nothing spikes, nothing sags — the lifetime ledger agrees, and the card reads strong from every angle. The kind of regular every fight is better for having.

bergenviii.text: BergenVIII plays the honest middle: sits above the average line comfortably, brisk on the trigger, and even-keeled when the heat rises. The matchup record sits mid-pack, a half-step behind the lifetime board, and the accuracy sits below average. Nothing flashy, nothing fragile — just a regular who shows up, reads the fight, and holds their ground.

beanoffurync1.text: BeanOfFuryNC1 brings pace and pressure: above average across the matchup card, with a brisk tempo that keeps fights moving. The punch fades when the opposition gets hardest, the single flaw in an otherwise strong card. Lifetime numbers back the matchups, and the aim stays honest without chasing headshots.

borgeninc.text: Since 2012, BoRGeNinc has played the long game: unhurried on the trigger, patient to a fault, and devastating once the fight is actually joined. The duel tally runs near the very top, the resistance is top-tier, and a lifetime of fighting shows the same steel. Slow to start, ruthless to finish — a veteran whose pace hides the punch.

beepbooprogerroger.text: BeepBoopRogerRoger wins fights with placement more than pace. The tempo sits around the middle, and the bravery mark does too, but the accuracy lands in the top bracket and the resistance holds well above average. The matchup figures land well above average, while the lifetime kill-death line agrees. A precise regular who picks the right moments and rarely wastes a shot.

blackoutgamer.text: Blackoutgamer carries a strong, rounded card: adjusted marks well above average, a brisk pace, and aim and headshots in the same bracket. The lifetime rating sits higher still, while the public kill-death line lands mid-pack. Against the hardest third the results settle into the middle ground instead of falling away. A dependable regular with no glaring crack in the armour.

brankovsk.text: Brankovsk keeps the pressure on from the first exchange: ahead of the pack across the matchup board, with a brisk tempo and steady aim. The edge softens when the opposition turns up the heat, the one wrinkle in an otherwise strong card. Lifetime numbers match the matchups, marking a reliable regular who rarely gives a fight away.

bringmemydakadakaboyz.text: BringMeMyDakaDakaBoyz plays loud and fast: ahead of the average in the matchups, with a brisk tempo and a lifetime kill-death record that lands mid-pack. The edge collapses when the strongest opponents show up, the sharpest drop in the card. A bold regular whose best work comes against ordinary opposition.

badbotanist.text: BadBotanist fires rarely and wins almost every duel they take: near the bottom on pace, deliberate to a fault, and patient when the fighting turns hardest. The matchup record stands at the very peak, and the resistance does too — they shrug off pressure that drops most fighters. The lifetime board agrees at the top, even as the IvI line sits below average. A study in patience: almost nothing spent, almost everything won.

bosscreinvs.text: BossCreinVS plays a brisk, accurate game: well above average on the pace and the aim, with the lifetime board to match, while the matchup tally reads mid-pack. When the opposition sharpens most, the output softens a touch — the one wrinkle on the card. A strong regular who shoots straight and keeps the tempo up.

bhasty.text: Bhasty plays a measured game with a sharp eye, landing comfortably above the middle overall. Unhurried on the trigger, and brave as the opposition stiffens. The headshot share sits well above average — the clearest strength on the card. Against the hardest opposition the results fade a little, and the head-to-head ledger reads middling. The career numbers lean a touch kinder than the matchups. A calm regular with a precise finish.

bobbib1llibob.text: BobbiB1lliBob plays a fast, front-foot game, well above the middle on almost every count. Quick on the tempo, and bold as the opposition stiffens. Against the hardest opposition the results drop off sharply — the one soft spot in an otherwise strong card. The head-to-head ledger sits above average, and the career numbers agree. A lively regular whose best work comes against the merely mortal.

bzzbbql.text: BZZBBQL plays a loud, fast game, comfortably above the middle on nearly every count, keeping a brisk pace and bold while the opposition stiffens. Lifetime IvI sits just under the summit, and the headshot share is clearly above the middle too. Once the opposition reaches its hardest, the results drop off sharply — the one soft spot in a bright showing. A strong regular who shines brightest when the fight is theirs to choose.

blibliblib.text: Blibliblib keeps the fight honest: sitting clear of the ordinary, patient on the trigger, and calm when the fighting gets rough. The aim runs above ordinary, their face-to-face showings run above the middle. The lifetime view matches. A regular who does the quiet work well and never asks for the spotlight.

buffer1aa.text: buffer1aa plays a tidy, well-rounded game: above the middle in the ways that matter, quick-handed, and collected when the fighting toughens. Their head-to-head ledger sits mid-pack, but the lifetime view runs a touch higher. A regular who does a little of everything well — and whose consistency is the whole point.

badbotru.text: Since 2015, BaDBoTru has played a measured, precise game: a clear notch above the pack in the matchups, unruffled as the fighting gets harder, and accurate enough that the shots that land tend to count. The tempo stays unhurried, and the sharpest opposition takes a little shine off the edge, the one wrinkle in a long, solid career. A veteran who still turns up and still makes every fight cost something.

bigdog43.text: bigdog43 is barely a week into the story and already turning heads: well above average overall, tough to move in a straight fight, and quick enough to keep the pressure on. The headshots land a clear step above the middle, though the aim itself is still finding its range. Against the very strongest opposition the edge dips sharply — early days, and that is exactly where a new account gets tested. A young regular with a bright first week behind them.

barn3tnc.text: Barn3tNC barely changes gear no matter who stands across the field: the same steady output against soft opposition and hard opposition alike makes them one of the most consistent fighters around. Their resistance holds up well, and the duel returns sit comfortably above average. Aim runs below the middle, yet the results rarely wobble.

beeziejenkins2.text: BeezieJenkins2 wins the fights that come to them and shrugs off opponents who kill fast, standing tall among the toughest company. In direct exchanges they come out ahead more often than not, and the shots that land tend to find the head. The pace is unhurried, though, and harder fights wear the edge down a little. A steady, well-above-average regular whose lifetime board leans the same way.

beamerbot.text: BeamerBot never slows down: the tempo runs near the very top, the aim stays clean, and the pressure keeps coming. The matchup return sits mid-pack, and the form sags against the fiercest opposition, so the engine runs hotter than the duels do. The lifetime figures match the busy style, and the finish stays sharp: a relentless regular who sets the pace.

belbiy.text: BelbIy has been a reliable presence since 2015: well above average overall, unshaken when the fight gets harder, and hard to put down. The pace stays brisk and the lifetime tally sits a little hotter than the matchups. Duel by duel they sit in the middle of the pack, while the headshots and the lifetime IvI both trail behind. A veteran regular who does the quiet work and keeps the fight honest.

blutulb.text: BlutulB wins fights nobody would expect them to: well above average overall, with head-to-head results near the very top and a lifetime tally to match. The staying power sits near the very top too, and the edge holds up when the fight gets hardest. The pace crawls, the aim wanders near the bottom, and the headshots barely show up. A patient regular who proves that slow and stubborn beats fast and flashy.

borgr02.text: Borgr02 plays at full throttle and makes it look easy: well above average overall, quick on their feet, and braver as the enemies get stronger. The aim runs true more often than most, and the pace never lets up. In the thick of a duel they trade evenly with the pack, while the lifetime tally edges a little higher. A regular already playing like a fixture.

bluechili3.text: bluechili3 has been a fixture since 2013: well above average overall, hard to move in a straight fight, and a matchup record in the middle. The tempo runs a little hotter than the rest of the game, while the lifetime figures rest in the middle too. A long-serving regular who turns up, holds the line, and never makes it easy.

busiki02.text: Since 2017, Busiki02 has played a fast, punchy game, and the all-round mark sits well above average: a brisk tempo, and a matchup record that sits comfortably above the middle. The lifetime kill-death figures run even hotter, though the lifetime IvI line sits low, a split that marks a player who wins fights without chasing the hardest ones. When the going gets hardest, the touch fades a little — the one wrinkle in a long, lively career.

beanofrage.text: BeanOfRage is brand new to the game, and already plays like they belong: well above average across the board, with a lively tempo and steady nerve when the opposition hardens. The matchup record lands above average, and the accuracy clears mid-pack. Against the fiercest opposition the form dips, the lone soft spot in an early story. Early read, but the opening chapters already impress.

brnsa.text: brnsa is barely three weeks in, and already the matchups belong to them: a matchup kill-death return sitting top shelf, well above average overall, and unshaken while the enemies get stronger. They shrug off punishment better than most, and the headshots keep finding their mark. The toughest third drags the results down sharply, and the lifetime line sits mid-pack. Early read, but the first weeks carry real weight.

buffer2aa.text: buffer2aa is still early in the story, and already there is no weak spot: well above average across the whole picture, fast through every exchange, and unmoved as the field gets tougher. The headshots land where they count, the pace stays brisk, and the results stay firm against stronger opposition. A young account, so the tale is young — but the opening pages already read like a regular who belongs.
